title.narrative: Protection against unacceptable forms of work is strengthened, in particular Forced Labour and Child Labour

description.narrative: The most recent ILO estimates showed that 1.1 million fewer women and men were employed in the country following the military take over. Employment remained low with the quality of jobs is deteriorating. Women have been more affected than men overall. These estimates cover the entire labour force of Myanmar, including formal and informal economy workers. The trends in Child Labour in the country from ILO publication in 2024 indicate a worrying increase in child labour driven by heightened poverty, displacement and security concerns. Children increasingly being drawn into hazardous forms of work, including forced recruitment into armed conflict and criminal activities. The country is witnessing more children drop out and fewer children enrol in education. In the post military takeover, children as young as 8 years old are engage in full time job. ILO is focusing on strengthening the capacity of social partners and community-based organizations to eliminate child labour in Myanmar. The National Action Plan (NAP) on elimination of child labour was launched with the assistance from ILO in 2019. The overarching goal of the NAP was established as “by 2030, all boys and girls in Myanmar are effectively prevented and protected from child labour, especially in its worse forms”. The list of the worse form of child labour was developed prior to the military take over. With the support from governments of UK, US and Japan, ILO developed a Child Labour Monitoring System (CLMS). This system function as monitoring tools and data collection for direct intervention support to families with child labour. Child Labour Elimination Tools and guidebooks were developed, and TOT were organized for social partners, Implementation Partners and Civil Society Organization. The ILO e-campus also serves as platform for public to learn about Child Labour and receive guidance from ILO experts.
